newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet on Monday, Veterans Day, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Cattle owners were asking $73.00 to $74.00 per cwt, but no packer bids were reported. Bids Tuesday were expected to surface at $72.00, unchanged from last week's trade.

Showlists this week were estimated larger than last week, but a large number of cattle on the lists remained 'green' or unfinished following aggressive sales last month 20 to 30 days ahead of schedule, the sources said.

The showlist for Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots was pegged near 60,000 head, up 3,000 head from last week, trade sources said. The Kansas showlist was estimated near 72,000 head, up 10,000 from last week.
At least four major beef packing plants were closed in observance of Monday's Veterans Day holiday.
IBP said its plants at Amarillo, Texas, Emporia, Kan., and West Point, Neb. would be closed. National Beef Packing also said its Liberal, Kansas, plant would be closed.
